title: Precipitation‐mediated asymmetric fitness consequences of nectar robbing in distylous Primula florindae
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Flowers with deep corollas are frequently associated with nectar robbing, a behaviour that often reduces pollen transfer and seed production. Robbing scars, however, may further affect plant reproductive success through rainwater entry into corolla tubes. In distylous species, the reciprocal positioning of stigmas and anthers in long- and short-styled morphs may create unequal exposure to incoming water and thereby impose morph-specific precipitation-mediated fitness costs. We used 2-year field manipulations in one focal population of distylous Primula florindae, manipulating nectar robbing in both years and additionally manipulating pollination success in a full-factorial design in 2024, to investigate how robbing associated with rainwater affects female fitness and interacts with legitimate visitation to shape phenotypic selection on floral traits. We further combined precipitation data, floral trait measurements and behavioural observations of the dominant visitor Bombus kashmirensis to explore the ecological context associated with the observed shift from legitimate visitation to nectar robbing. Our manipulations revealed that robbing significantly reduced seed production independently of pollen limitation. This reduction was stronger in long-styled plants, and the contrast between morphs was more pronounced in the wetter year, consistent with differential water exposure in pendant flowers: the long-styled stigma lies below upward-facing robbing holes, where water may accumulate and submerge it, whereas the short-styled stigma lies deeper within the corolla tube but spatially above this accumulation zone. Furthermore, legitimate visitation and nectar robbing exerted complex, interactive selective pressures across floral traits, with illegitimate visitation driving accentuated, morph-specific divergent selection on corolla length. However, neither type of visitation alone, nor both types combined, fully explained the net selection on this trait, suggesting additional selective agents. Observational evidence indicated that robbing onset was associated with elevated pre-onset rainfall, unusually long corollas and greater foraging efficiency during secondary robbing, although these relationships remain inferential. In summary, our study provides experimental evidence that nectar robbing can turn floral damage into a precipitation-mediated fitness cost, offering new insights into how nectar robbing affects plant fitness. More broadly, our results suggest that climatic factors can mediate plant–visitor interactions along the mutualism–antagonism continuum and contribute to context-dependent adaptive trajectories.

摘要

花冠筒较长的花往往更易发生盗蜜，而盗蜜通常会降低花粉转移效率和种子产量。然而，盗蜜留下的伤痕还可能通过使雨水进入花冠筒，进一步影响植物的繁殖成功。在二型花柱植物中，长、短花柱型的柱头和花药呈交互式雌雄异位排列，这种繁殖器官位置差异可能导致两种花型不同程度地暴露于进入花内的雨水中，进而产生花型特异性的降水介导适合度代价。 本研究以一个二型花柱巨伞钟报春(Primula florindae)群体为对象，开展了连续两年的野外操控实验:两年均操控盗蜜，2024年进一步采用全因子设计同时操控盗蜜和授粉成功，以检验与雨水进入相关的盗蜜如何影响雌性适合度，以及盗蜜如何与合法访花相互作用，共同塑造对花部性状的表型选择。我们还结合降水数据、花部性状测量以及优势访花者克什米尔熊蜂(Bombus kashmirensis)的行为观察，探讨所观察到的合法访花向盗蜜转变的生态背景。 操控实验表明，盗蜜显著降低了种子产量，且这一效应独立于花粉限制。种子产量的下降在长花柱型中更为显著，而且两种花型之间的差异在较湿年份更加明显，这与下垂花朵中两种花型对雨水的暴露差异一致:长花柱型的柱头位于朝上的盗蜜孔下方，雨水可能在此积聚并淹没柱头；短花柱型的柱头虽然位于花冠筒更深处，但在空间位置上高于这一积水区域。 此外，合法访花和盗蜜对多个花部性状施加了复杂且相互作用的选择压力，其中盗蜜进一步强化了针对花冠长度的花型特异性分化选择。然而，无论合法访花或盗蜜单独作用，还是二者共同作用，都不能完全解释该性状的净选择格局，表明可能还存在其他选择因子。 观察性证据表明，盗蜜的开始与盗蜜发生前较高的降雨量、异常偏长的花冠以及次级盗蜜过程中较高的觅食效率相关，但这些关系仍属于推断性证据。 总之，本研究提供了实验证据，表明盗蜜可将花部损伤转化为降水介导的适合度代价，从而为理解盗蜜如何影响植物适合度提供了新的视角。更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，气候因子能够介导植物—访花者相互作用在互利—拮抗连续谱上的表现，并可能影响情境依赖的适应性演化轨迹。
